title: Growing-Domain Turing Topology
summary: A topology-aware reaction-diffusion study tracks pattern splitting and mode selection as a synthetic tissue domain grows.

publish_assets.alt: Space-time activator field, domain length, peak count, and final pattern for a growing-domain Turing simulation.
publish_assets.caption: A smooth growth pulse produces discrete peak-splitting events in the synthetic Schnakenberg system.

publish_assets.alt: Three annotated heatmaps of final peak count, topology events, and spectral disorder over growth and kinetic parameters.
publish_assets.caption: Pattern identity depends jointly on growth rate and kinetic margin.

publish_assets.alt: Dispersion relation and coupled grid-time refinement for the growing-domain reaction-diffusion solver.
publish_assets.caption: The fixed-domain instability baseline and refinement study bound the numerical interpretation.

research_question: Which growth and kinetic regimes preserve pattern identity, and which generate splitting, merging, or mode loss?
limitations: No organism is fitted or identified.
Topology is represented by one-dimensional peak events.
Parameter conclusions are conditional on the Schnakenberg family.
documentation_excerpt: A verified synthetic study of how continuous and pulsed domain growth rewrite Turing-pattern identity.

title: Heterogeneous Morphoelastic Folding
summary: A reduced nonlinear-elasticity model tests whether weak growth and stiffness heterogeneity can steer fold location and count.

publish_assets.alt: Four reduced tissue-strip shapes under homogeneous and phase-shifted heterogeneous growth fields.
publish_assets.caption: Weak heterogeneity relocates or suppresses folds while preserving endpoint constraints.

publish_assets.alt: Annotated maps of fold-targeting error, peak curvature, and fold count across heterogeneity amplitude and phase.
publish_assets.caption: Fold steering depends on the phase between load and stiffness fields.

publish_assets.alt: Steering-curvature frontier, homogeneous buckling threshold, and quadrature-refinement panels.
publish_assets.caption: Design claims are checked against the analytical threshold and grid refinement.

research_question: Can weak heterogeneity steer growth-induced folds without increasing the peak deformation proxy?
limitations: The strip is a reduced beam, not a calibrated tissue.
Peak curvature is a model proxy rather than a biological damage threshold.
Three-dimensional remodelling and material turnover are omitted.
documentation_excerpt: An energy-based continuum study of phase-controlled folding under heterogeneous growth and stiffness.

title: Robust Safe Envelope for an Exothermic CSTR
summary: A bifurcation and uncertainty study quantifies the production cost of avoiding hot or multiple stable reactor equilibria.

publish_assets.alt: Stable and unstable CSTR equilibrium-temperature branches against coolant temperature.
publish_assets.caption: Equilibrium multiplicity makes coolant selection a branch-selection problem.

publish_assets.alt: Stress-test risk and nominal yield maps over residence time and coolant temperature.
publish_assets.caption: The productive operating region and the robust region do not coincide.

publish_assets.alt: Yield-risk frontier, cost-of-robustness bars, and independent equilibrium checks.
publish_assets.caption: The selected robust point sacrifices nominal yield to reduce the declared synthetic risk.

data_type: Synthetic CSTR parameters and uncertainty scenarios
research_question: What nominal production is sacrificed when the hot-state and multiplicity stress-test risk is constrained?
limitations: The stress-test fraction is not a calibrated accident probability.
Parameters do not represent a named industrial plant.
Spatial gradients and control-actuator dynamics are omitted.
documentation_excerpt: A verified synthetic reactor study connecting steady-state multiplicity, uncertainty, and production trade-offs.

title: Positive and Conservative Time Stepping
summary: A stiff transfer-network benchmark tests when explicit solvers create negative mass and what a conservative positive update costs.

publish_assets.alt: Euler, RK4, and positive implicit trajectories for a stiff conservative three-state transfer.
publish_assets.caption: Coarse explicit steps can create impossible negative mass even when total mass is formally conserved.

publish_assets.alt: Three feasibility maps over stiffness and time step for Euler, RK4, and a positive implicit method.
publish_assets.caption: The positive update preserves non-negativity throughout the tested grid.

publish_assets.alt: Cost-error, invariant-drift, and adaptive-tolerance panels for conservative time integration.
publish_assets.caption: Physical feasibility has an explicit computational and accuracy trade-off.

research_question: When do explicit schemes violate non-negativity, and what error-cost trade-off accompanies a positive conservative update?
limitations: The benchmark networks are linear.
No universal method ranking is claimed.
Nonconservative forcing and general nonlinear chemistry are outside scope.
documentation_excerpt: A matrix-exponential-verified benchmark where feasibility and invariant preservation are assessed alongside error.

title: Incentives and the Reliability of a Scientific Field
summary: An evolutionary agent model explores novelty, rigour, and replication incentives as a reliability-discovery trade-off.

publish_assets.alt: Two policy-simplex maps showing claim reliability and true discovery rate under novelty, rigour, and replication weights.
publish_assets.caption: No single incentive corner maximises both reliability and discovery in the synthetic field.

publish_assets.alt: Reliability-discovery frontier, mean-field cross-check, and population-size sensitivity.
publish_assets.caption: The policy trade-off is checked across seed ensembles, a mean-field approximation, and field size.

publish_assets.alt: Time series of evolved novelty, rigour, replication propensity, and field reliability under three policies.
publish_assets.caption: Incentives reshape laboratory strategies before changing field-level reliability.

data_type: Synthetic laboratories, claims, and replication events
research_question: Which incentive mixes improve reliability without collapsing the rate of true discovery?
limitations: Parameters are not fitted to a real discipline.
Publication and replication are simplified behavioural rules.
The model is a thought experiment rather than a policy forecast.
documentation_excerpt: An evolutionary policy laboratory for studying how publication rewards select scientific strategies.

title: Robust Hedging under Rough Volatility and Costs
summary: A held-out stress study selects a no-trade delta band across uncertain roughness, volatility, and transaction-cost regimes.

publish_assets.alt: Synthetic asset and volatility paths with loss distributions and turnover-loss comparison.
publish_assets.caption: Rough volatility and transaction costs turn frequent delta correction into a turnover problem.

publish_assets.alt: Annotated held-out CVaR and turnover matrices for full delta, fixed-band, and robust-band hedging.
publish_assets.caption: One frozen band is evaluated across unseen roughness and cost regimes.

publish_assets.alt: Robust tuning objective, tail-risk-turnover frontier, and time-grid martingale diagnostics.
publish_assets.caption: The selected band reduces held-out turnover and tail loss within the synthetic simulator.

data_type: Synthetic rough-volatility paths and option-hedging records
research_question: Can a frozen uncertainty-aware no-trade band reduce held-out tail loss and turnover under model and cost misspecification?
limitations: No market data are fitted.
The simulator is not a complete rough-volatility pricing model.
Results are not investment advice or evidence of deployable performance.
documentation_excerpt: A leakage-aware synthetic hedge stress test with an explicit martingale diagnostic and frozen robust policy.

title: Intervention-Calibrated Neural ODEs

publish_assets.alt: True and ensemble-predicted toggle-switch trajectories under strong and suppressive held-out interventions.
publish_assets.caption: Structural constraints alter extrapolation but do not automatically calibrate uncertainty.

publish_assets.alt: Generating, unconstrained, and sign-structured learned phase fields for a synthetic gene toggle.
publish_assets.caption: Intervention forecasts inherit the geometry and failure modes of the learned vector field.

publish_assets.alt: Held-out trajectory error, interval coverage, and ODE-solver tolerance panels.
publish_assets.caption: Lower trajectory error does not guarantee calibrated uncertainty under intervention shift.

title: Dimensionally Constrained Equation Discovery
summary: A controlled symbolic-search benchmark measures exact recovery, search-space reduction, and unit robustness under scarce noisy data.

publish_assets.alt: Exact equation-recovery curves for raw and dimensionally filtered searches across four benchmarks.
publish_assets.caption: Dimensional filtering helps only when physical dimensions remove plausible alternatives.

publish_assets.alt: Candidate cloud, adversarial unit-shift error, and search-space-reduction panels.
publish_assets.caption: Unit consistency acts as both a search prior and an adversarial validity test.

publish_assets.alt: Bootstrap winner frequencies for raw and dimensionally constrained drag equations.
publish_assets.caption: Constraint filtering changes the genealogy of equations selected from noisy small samples.

research_question: How much do dimensional invariants improve compact-equation recovery under small noisy samples?

Benchmarks are controlled rather than discoveries.
The dimensionless negative control shows where filtering has no leverage.
documentation_excerpt: An auditable symbolic-search experiment where unit changes expose dimensionally invalid small-sample winners.

title: Sparse Wave Blocking in Excitable Media
summary: A sensor-triggered local controller is tuned and stress-tested for blocking travelling waves in a generic excitable medium.

publish_assets.alt: Uncontrolled and locally controlled excitation-wave fields with the corresponding applied current.
publish_assets.caption: A sensor-triggered local refractory barrier intercepts the representative travelling wave.

publish_assets.alt: Training maps of blocking probability and control energy over pulse amplitude and duration.
publish_assets.caption: The lowest-energy reliable policy lies near a narrow blocking boundary.

publish_assets.alt: Energy-success frontier, held-out policy comparison, and grid-time refinement.
publish_assets.caption: The local controller is compared with no control and periodic global forcing under unseen conduction and delay scenarios.

The control is not a medical intervention proposal.
Only one-dimensional propagation and one sensor-actuator pair are represented.

title: Sequential Nonlinear Model Discrimination
summary: A Bayesian experiment-design benchmark selects forcing conditions to separate Van der Pol, Rayleigh, and Duffing mechanisms.

publish_assets.alt: Robust predictive-separation scores over forcing amplitude and frequency, with response magnitude comparison.
publish_assets.caption: The most informative forcing is not simply the largest forcing.

publish_assets.alt: Posterior probability paths for three true oscillator families under fixed, adaptive, and oracle experiment schedules.
publish_assets.caption: Adaptive experiments contract different model posteriors at different rates.

publish_assets.alt: Identification accuracy, Brier score, and solver-tolerance panels.
publish_assets.caption: Adaptive design is judged by probability quality as well as final model labels.

limitations: The comparison is closed to three model families.
True parameters are drawn from declared synthetic priors.
The oracle is an upper comparison and not an implementable policy.

title: Occupancy-Aware Classroom Ventilation
summary: A shared-capacity predictive-control benchmark studies classroom CO2 exposure when timetables are wrong and ventilation capacity is temporarily derated.

publish_assets.alt: Two academic line-and-interval charts comparing person-weighted classroom CO2 exposure and fan-energy proxy across nominal, room-change, capacity-derating, and combined-stress conditions.
publish_assets.caption: Four controllers are evaluated on 120 matched synthetic days per condition; error bars are bootstrap 95% intervals.

publish_assets.alt: A three-classroom shared-fan schematic beside CO2 and occupancy traces for a representative combined-stress school day.
publish_assets.caption: The shared command budget couples three well-mixed classroom mass balances under time-varying occupancy.

publish_assets.alt: Five-stage methodology diagram from timetable and measured state through short forecasting, constrained airflow allocation, and room-change plus capacity stress testing.
publish_assets.caption: The evidence pipeline separates occupancy information, controller state, predictive allocation, and stress evaluation.

publish_assets.alt: A combined-stress exposure-energy trade-off chart and a sensitivity plot showing exposure and fan energy as the occupancy forecast buffer increases.
publish_assets.caption: The uncertainty buffer produces a modest exposure reduction while increasing the fan-energy proxy.

data_type: Synthetic three-classroom timetable, occupancy perturbations, and well-mixed CO2 trajectories
research_question: Can short-horizon airflow allocation reduce occupied CO2 exposure when room use and shared ventilation capacity depart from the timetable, and what energy cost accompanies an occupancy buffer?
limitations: The rooms are well-mixed synthetic zones rather than calibrated classrooms or a commissioned air-handling system.
The 1000 ppm line is a benchmark control target and not a universal health, safety, or compliance threshold.
Fan energy and ventilation thermal load are proxies; aerosols, filtration, infection risk, and health outcomes are not modelled.
documentation_excerpt: This reproducible benchmark compares fixed, reactive, and predictive airflow allocation when three classrooms share limited capacity and actual room use departs from the timetable.

title: Graph-Calibrated Battery Thermal Early Warning
summary: A sequential graph-CUSUM study for warning of local battery-pack thermal faults under temperature-sensor drift and dropout.

publish_assets.alt: Two IEEE-oriented line-and-interval charts comparing timely thermal-fault detection and median warning lead time across nominal, sensor-drift, sensor-dropout, and combined conditions.
publish_assets.caption: Four detectors are evaluated on matched synthetic trajectories; proportion intervals are Wilson 95% intervals and lead-time intervals are bootstrap 95% intervals.

publish_assets.alt: A labelled 4 by 4 battery thermal network beside a representative fault trajectory with fault onset, graph-CUSUM alarm, and 60 degree simulation boundary.
publish_assets.caption: The benchmark represents cells as a coupled thermal graph and evaluates whether an alarm arrives before the study boundary.

publish_assets.alt: Five-stage academic methodology diagram from coupled thermal simulation through residual construction, graph evidence pooling, sequential testing, and drift-dropout stress evaluation.
publish_assets.caption: Only the graph-evidence and calibrated sequential-test stages are proposed; calibration and evaluation use disjoint seed ranges.

publish_assets.alt: An interval plot of false-alarm rate against positive sensor drift and a hatched ablation chart under combined drift and sensor dropout.
publish_assets.caption: The robustness sweep and ablation expose the method's detection-versus-false-alarm trade-off instead of reporting accuracy alone.

data_type: Synthetic 4 x 4 coupled thermal network with generated drift, dropout, and local-fault trajectories
research_question: Can common-mode removal and graph-neighbour pooling improve warning before a synthetic battery-pack temperature boundary while keeping false alarms near a held-out calibration target?
limitations: The thermal network is a transparent numerical proxy rather than a chemistry-specific electrochemical or abuse-test model.
The 60 degree Celsius endpoint is a study boundary, not a universal thermal-runaway or safety threshold.
The reported intervals overlap for several comparisons and no instrumented module or deployed battery-management system is evaluated.
documentation_excerpt: This controlled benchmark tests whether graph-aware sequential evidence can preserve warning performance when one battery temperature channel drifts or becomes unavailable.

title: Resilient Water-Network Leak Localisation
summary: A dropout-aware pressure-sensor placement study for localising leaks under measurement noise and single-sensor failure.

publish_assets.alt: Two IEEE-style line charts comparing leak-localisation accuracy across pressure noise and sensor dropout for four placement methods.
publish_assets.caption: The proposed dropout-aware placement is compared with random, degree-centrality, and nominal greedy layouts; error bars show Wilson 95% intervals.

publish_assets.alt: Five-stage IEEE-style methodology diagram from synthetic network construction through leak signatures, dropout-aware sensor placement, localisation, and stress evaluation.
publish_assets.caption: The reproducible evidence pipeline separates the proposed placement step from signature generation, localisation, and Monte Carlo evaluation.

publish_assets.alt: Side-by-side water-network diagrams comparing nominal greedy and dropout-aware pressure sensor locations.
publish_assets.caption: Nominal and dropout-aware sensor layouts on the 36-node synthetic network. The proposed objective spreads measurements across diagnostically distinct regions after sensor loss.

publish_assets.alt: Bar charts of dropout-aware signature separation and top-one and top-three leak-localisation accuracy under the designated stress test.
publish_assets.caption: Ablation and stress test at 8% relative pressure noise and 40% probability of one sensor dropout.

data_type: Synthetic hydraulic-inspired network and generated Monte Carlo benchmark
research_question: Can pressure sensors selected for lower-tail leak-signature separation retain localisation performance when measurements are noisy and one sensor may fail?
limitations: The graph-Laplacian response is a controlled proxy rather than an EPANET or field-calibrated hydraulic model.
Only one unavailable sensor, independent Gaussian noise, and one leak at a time are represented.
The reported advantage is not uniform across every noise level and does not establish field performance.
documentation_excerpt: This reproducible synthetic study tests whether dropout-aware pressure-sensor placement preserves leak-localisation performance when measurements are noisy and one sensor is unavailable.

title: Adaptive Harvesting under Allee-Effect Risk
summary: A verified stochastic population study compares fixed, proportional, and refuge-based harvesting when temporary declines can cross a nonlinear collapse threshold.

publish_assets.alt: Population trajectories under fixed-quota, proportional, and threshold-adaptive harvesting with critical abundance levels marked.
publish_assets.caption: A temporary decline becomes irreversible after the simulated stock crosses the strong-Allee threshold.

publish_assets.alt: Finite-horizon collapse probability across normalized harvesting intensity for three policy families.
publish_assets.caption: The fixed and proportional controls exhibit abrupt risk cliffs in the tested grid.

publish_assets.alt: Estimated finite-horizon collapse probability against mean realized yield for three harvesting policies.
publish_assets.caption: The refuge rule changes the tested risk-yield frontier by making extraction depend on current abundance.

publish_assets.alt: Comparative synthetic outcomes for fixed-quota, proportional, and threshold-adaptive harvesting.
publish_assets.caption: A policy is a state-to-action map, not merely a target harvest level.

research_question: Which feedback rule preserves useful harvest while limiting finite-horizon collapse risk near a strong Allee threshold?
limitations: The model is not calibrated to a species or fishery.
Zero observed collapses in a finite Monte Carlo grid does not imply zero true or long-run risk.
Observation error, delayed control, age structure, and spatial dynamics are omitted.
documentation_excerpt: A reviewed public-evidence wrapper for a stochastic harvesting experiment.

title: Genetic Drift, Selection, and Migration
summary: A verified Wright–Fisher simulation study separates the probability of eventual fixation from the preservation of diversity under selection, migration, and demographic bottlenecks.

publish_assets.alt: Heat map of simulated fixation probability across population size and selection coefficient.
publish_assets.caption: Population size changes how strongly sampling noise competes with selection.

publish_assets.alt: Simulated fixation probabilities compared with the Kimura diffusion approximation.
publish_assets.caption: The theoretical curve is used as a validation target, not as a replacement for uncertainty estimates.

publish_assets.alt: Allele-frequency outcomes showing migration opposing local selection in a two-population experiment.
publish_assets.caption: Gene flow can replenish a locally disfavoured allele and maintain a migration-selection balance.

publish_assets.alt: Heterozygosity trajectories with and without a temporary population bottleneck.
publish_assets.caption: A brief bottleneck leaves a persistent diversity deficit after census size recovers.

research_question: When do drift, selection, migration, and bottlenecks dominate the fate of a newly introduced allele and the diversity around it?
limitations: The simulations are idealized Wright–Fisher experiments rather than estimates for a named population.
Linked selection, recombination, mutation during fixation runs, and genomic ascertainment are outside scope.
Fixation probability and time-to-fixation are distinct quantities.
documentation_excerpt: A reviewed public-evidence wrapper for the population-genetic simulations.

title: Phylogenetic Model Misspecification
summary: A verified quartet simulation demonstrates how increasing sequence length can make a wrong tree more stable when the analysis model cannot represent compositional heterogeneity.

publish_assets.alt: Correct quartet recovery against sequence length under a compositionally heterogeneous generating process.
publish_assets.caption: More sites reduce sampling noise while concentrating misspecified distances on the wrong split.

publish_assets.alt: Tree-recovery rates by generating scenario, distance estimator, and sequence length.
publish_assets.caption: Methods that converge under the homogeneous control can fail under the designed heterogeneous process.

publish_assets.alt: Recovery comparison across composition contrast and long-branch severity.
publish_assets.caption: Regularized log-det is more robust in much of the tested region but is not universally correct.

publish_assets.alt: Bootstrap support for true and wrong quartet splits under three distance estimators.
publish_assets.caption: High bootstrap support measures stability conditional on the analysis pipeline, not model adequacy.

research_question: Can more DNA increase confidence in the wrong topology when the inference model is structurally misspecified?
limitations: The quartet and heterogeneous process are designed demonstrations.
The results do not establish that regularized log-det is universally superior.
Empirical phylogenomics involves additional taxa, partitions, recombination, and alignment uncertainty.
documentation_excerpt: A reviewed public-evidence wrapper for a model-adequacy demonstration.

title: Real-Time sEMG Conditioning with Tracked Harmonic Cancellation

publish_assets.alt: Streaming sEMG conditioning pipeline with a separate supervisory mains-frequency tracker.
publish_assets.caption: The architecture keeps the per-sample path causal while updating interference frequency periodically.

publish_assets.alt: Synthetic reconstruction SNR and residual rest-envelope comparisons across cancellation modes.
publish_assets.caption: Tracked harmonic cancellation improves the two declared synthetic benchmarks relative to fixed or absent cancellation.

publish_assets.alt: Host-Python fast-path timing and exponential-envelope memory summaries.
publish_assets.caption: Reference latency and smoothing memory are reported separately because they answer different design questions.

title: Non-isothermal CSTR Hysteresis
summary: A verified nonlinear reactor study maps equilibrium multiplicity, ignition and extinction hysteresis, competing basins of attraction, and critical slowing near a thermal fold.

publish_assets.alt: S-shaped equilibrium temperature branch of a non-isothermal CSTR with stable and unstable segments and two folds.
publish_assets.caption: The same coolant setting can support cold, intermediate, and hot equilibria, but only the outer branches are stable.

publish_assets.alt: Quasistatic warming and cooling paths following different stable branches of the CSTR equilibrium diagram.
publish_assets.caption: Ignition and extinction occur at different coolant settings because each stable branch persists until its own fold.

publish_assets.alt: Coolant and reactor temperature trajectories during a triangular coolant cycle.
publish_assets.caption: Finite relaxation creates delayed jumps during a dynamic coolant cycle.

publish_assets.alt: Initial-condition map showing cold and hot basins of attraction at a coolant value inside the multiplicity interval.
publish_assets.caption: Returning an input to its old value does not ensure recovery of the old internal state.

publish_assets.alt: Estimated linear recovery time increasing near the cold-branch ignition fold.
publish_assets.caption: The dominant recovery time rises as an eigenvalue approaches zero near the fold.

research_question: How do stability, path history, and recovery rate change as a non-isothermal reactor approaches thermal ignition or extinction?
limitations: The model is a dimensionless synthetic mechanism study rather than an industrial reactor calibration.
Mixing imperfection, transport delay, catalyst deactivation, multiple reactions, actuator limits, and parameter uncertainty are omitted.
Critical slowing is a mechanistic diagnostic, not a universal early-warning guarantee.
documentation_excerpt: A reviewed private-evidence wrapper for thermal multiplicity and hysteresis.

title: Publish-or-Perish and Method Selection
summary: A verified agent-based mechanism experiment examines how publication rewards, publication bias, replication audits, and failed-replication penalties select methodological effort.

publish_assets.alt: Methodological effort trajectories under publication-count, moderate-audit, and strong-replication regimes.
publish_assets.caption: Selection on publication count and selection under consequential replication audits move the effort distribution in opposite directions.

publish_assets.alt: False-discovery, expected replication, and publication-output outcomes for three simulated institutions.
publish_assets.caption: Paper volume and reliable information are different policy objectives.

publish_assets.alt: Heat map of final methodological effort by audit probability and failed-replication penalty.
publish_assets.caption: Audit frequency and consequence interact; neither lever is effective in isolation across the tested grid.

publish_assets.alt: Heat map of final false-discovery fraction by audit probability and failed-replication penalty.
publish_assets.caption: The reliability response mirrors the policy-dependent selection on effort.

publish_assets.alt: Selected methodological effort across publication-bias levels with and without a strong replication policy.
publish_assets.caption: Consequential audits reduce, but do not erase, sensitivity to the publication rule.

research_question: When laboratories inherit successful practices, which combinations of publication rewards and replication consequences select for reliable methods?
limitations: The results are generated by a stylised institutional model and are not estimates of any discipline or researcher population.
One scalar effort trait compresses heterogeneous research practices, resources, career stages, and strategic behaviour.
Policy outcomes depend on the declared truth base rate, publication rule, audit process, and selection mechanism.
documentation_excerpt: A reviewed private-evidence wrapper for selection on methodological effort.

title: Stochastic Genetic-Toggle Switching
summary: A verified deterministic-and-stochastic study connects toggle-circuit bistability to finite-copy-number switching, first-passage memory, stationary probability, and pulse control.

publish_assets.alt: Nullclines and trajectories of a mutually repressing genetic toggle with two stable equilibria and one saddle.
publish_assets.caption: The deterministic system supplies two memory states and a basin boundary.

publish_assets.alt: Representative Gillespie toggle trajectories at four molecular system sizes.
publish_assets.caption: Finite reaction noise creates rare crossings that a deterministic trajectory cannot make.

publish_assets.alt: Mean first-passage time and switch probability across five molecular system sizes.
publish_assets.caption: The same deterministic phase portrait can support very different stochastic memory lifetimes.

publish_assets.alt: Bimodal stationary distribution with peaks near the two deterministic stable expression states.
publish_assets.caption: A stochastic steady state is a probability distribution rather than a single equilibrium point.

publish_assets.alt: Toggle-switch success probability across induction pulse amplitudes and durations.
publish_assets.caption: Control at finite copy number is probabilistic and depends on both pulse amplitude and exposure time.

data_type: Controlled deterministic and stochastic circuit simulations
research_question: How does finite molecular copy number turn deterministic bistability into a memory with a measurable switching lifetime?

The pulse-control grid uses limited Monte Carlo replication and should not be read as a smooth optimum.

title: Michaelis-Menten QSSA Validity Atlas
summary: A verified 243-case parameter atlas measures where the Michaelis-Menten quasi-steady-state reduction agrees with full mass-action kinetics and where timing or trajectory error becomes material.

publish_assets.alt: Maximum normalized product error over enzyme-abundance and substrate-saturation parameters.
publish_assets.caption: Validity is a region in parameter and task space, not a single universal cutoff.

publish_assets.alt: Maximum product error versus the enzyme-abundance small parameter for several saturation levels.
publish_assets.caption: Small enzyme abundance improves the reduction, but the observed error also depends on substrate saturation.

publish_assets.alt: Full mass-action and QSSA product trajectories for good, borderline, and failure parameter sets.
publish_assets.caption: The initial complex-formation layer becomes consequential when time-scale separation weakens.

publish_assets.alt: Relative half-conversion timing error over the QSSA parameter grid.
publish_assets.caption: A reduction acceptable for product amplitude can still be inaccurate for event timing.

publish_assets.alt: Full enzyme-kinetic trajectory rapidly approaching and then following the QSSA slow manifold.
publish_assets.caption: The reduced law represents motion along an attracting lower-dimensional relation after a fast transient.

research_question: For which parameter regimes, outputs, and time horizons is the Michaelis-Menten QSSA an accurate replacement for the full mass-action mechanism?
limitations: The atlas is synthetic and does not estimate kinetic constants for a named enzyme.
Product inhibition, substrate inhibition, cooperative binding, diffusion, inactivation, and stochastic copy-number effects are outside scope.
The tested grid supports task-specific diagnostics, not a universal validity threshold.
documentation_excerpt: A reviewed private-evidence wrapper for a fast-slow model-reduction audit.
